owner: MES-97 (C1a), re-declared by MES-104 (C1b-i) to its 3 non-client rows
what_this_is: The AUTHORED adjudications the crosswalk is built from — one record per (ET-CC member, claim, OC check). Judgements are data with evidence; derivations are code. `tag`, `oc_key`, `shape` and `bucket` appear NOWHERE here: the generator derives all four through MCP.Conformance.MatchKey and refuses any edge whose stored form disagrees, so a stored edge cannot lie about its own axes or address a key it does not encode.

the_population_this_file_declares.rule: The ET-CC members C1a had adjudicated — a token or a contradicts_oc record — that are NOT on the client leg: 2 server and 1 none_determinable. C1a's 18 client rows moved to crosswalk-edges-client.json under MES-104's composition ruling; these 3 stayed, unchanged, and C1c (MES-105) absorbs them whole.

selector.what_this_is: The EXECUTABLE half of `rule`. The generator evaluates it against the source named below and requires the result to be SET-EQUAL, in both directions, to the population this file derives. Prose only becomes a guard when something can run it.
selector.why_it_must_name_a_file_other_than_this_: C1a derived its declared population by unioning the register_keys the edges file itself carried, so a dropped row did not violate the universe, it SHRANK it — measured on MES-99, both a dropped edge and a dropped declared_unmatched row built cleanly at 20 members with every set comparison still exact. A selector that read this file's own rows would be circular by another route.
selector.denotes: The 3 non-client members of C1a's original 21: MCP.Server.DispatchTest and MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTPStatelessTest (server, both carrying a contradicts_oc record) and MCP.IntegrationTest (none_determinable, carrying a token).
selector.why_none_of_and_not_an_enumeration_of_th: `leg` happens to take three values in B2b today, so `any_of[server, none_determinable]` would denote the same 3 rows. It would do so only while that remains true: a fourth leg value would silently drop its members out of this population, and nothing would go red. `none_of[client]` states the rule the prose states and carries no assumption about the field's range.
selector.c1b_and_c1c_declare_their_own: The selector is per-population and is read from this file, never hard-coded in the generator. C1c (MES-105) states the rule denoting the server leg rather than inheriting a literal 3.

the_population_this_file_declares.everything_else_is: not_yet_adjudicated — a THIRD state, distinct from bucket 1 ('we looked, there is no counterpart') and from A3 §6 state 4 ('nobody has adjudicated this member'). 260 ET-CC members and 159 in-denominator checks are in it. C1b (MES-104, client leg) and C1c (MES-105, server leg) own them.
the_population_this_file_declares.why_4_checks_and_not_2: C1a's original block explained the same thing over 14 checks and the same two rows carry it here. B2b's tokens address TWO of these four; the other two — HttpServerMethodNotFound404ping and HttpServerMethodNotFound404loggingsetLevel — enter through ONE member, MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTPStatelessTest's `initialize is gone -> -32022; ping/logging.setLevel -> -32601`. This is NOT new adjudication: match-relation.md §1's cardinality table names that member by file and line and rules it yields THREE edges, and §4's worked edge record publishes the ping edge complete with its two axes and its `:partial` shape. Dropping them would leave a member the ratified rule says has three claims contributing one, which is the collapse §1 forbids.
the_population_this_file_declares.the_fourth_check: `tool-add-numbers` / ToolAddNumbers, addressed by MCP.IntegrationTest — the none_determinable member. It is why this residual is 3 members and 4 checks rather than 2 and 3.
the_population_this_file_declares.no_check_population_is_declared_here: Deliberately. These 3 rows are a residual awaiting C1c, not a leg anyone claims totality over, and declaring a check population would put the rest of `server-stateless` into bucket 2 — asserting of each sibling check that we looked and found no ET counterpart, which nobody has. A file with no declared check population contributes none to bucket 2's universe; its checks are derived from its own edges, exactly as C1a did.

what_a_record_carries_and_why.member: MES-67's unit: module AND test name. The `register_key` is docs/conformance/etcc-row-key.md §1's key and is what joins this file to the register; it was extracted from the register, never typed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim: A3 §1's atom of matching — finer than a test, coarser than an assert. A member bundling claims contributes several edges and they are never collapsed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.tag: A3 §5's token. The generator DECODES and RESOLVES it against A1's manifest and derives the six-field oc_key from the resolution; it never accepts a key from this file.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.axes: One verdict per axis of the check's predicate, naming axes that must exist in the check's axis decomposition (A3's 13 or C1's 11). The generator refuses an axis name the decomposition does not contain — a verdict against an axis nobody extracted is a verdict about nothing.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.et_verdict: The member's own run verdict. Every member of this population is `green`: re-measured at 42e6b19 over the full suite, all 281 ET-CC members pass. So buckets 3 (green OC / red ET) and 6 (red in both) are EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION on this data — checked, and zero, with the predicate recorded.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.evidence: File, line and the assertion, for every axis verdict. Ruling 7: an address is not evidence, the bytes at it are.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.not_carried: No `oc_key`, no `shape`, no `bucket`, no OC verdict. All four are derived — the OC verdict from A1's committed per-check `status` at the accepted run, the rest through MatchKey.

how_a_silent_axis_was_decided: Conservatively, and the rule is stated rather than applied case by case: a claim counts as covering an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. A test asserting a tool's RESULT does not cover an axis about the ARGUMENTS' wire type, and a test asserting that a capability is ABSENT does not cover an axis about the SHAPE of a present one. This is match-relation.md §6's CG5 rule — a mention is not a discharge — turned on our own side of the relation. Where it was a judgement rather than a reading, the edge's `evidence` says so in those words.
the_all_silent_case: Four edges have EVERY axis silent. They are recorded and ESCALATED, never bucketed. A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis 'is no match, not a partial one'; generalised to N axes that is exactly this case, and A3 §3's table has no row for it — `shape_from_axes/1` would call it `:partial` and bucket 5 would swallow it. Dropping the edges instead would be worse: the member would then look edge-less and therefore bucket-1, asserting 'we looked and there is no counterpart' where the truth is 'there is a counterpart and our claim does not touch its predicate'. Escalation is A3 §7's own mechanism for a case the rule does not decide.

edges.claim: a tools/call to `add` with two numeric arguments is issued and returns their sum
edges.evidence: integration_test.exs:149-150 — `Client.call_tool(client, "add", %{"a" => 3, "b" => 4})` returns `"7"`. The call being made is asserted directly. The two type axes are NOT: the assertion is on the tool's RESULT, and a client sending `"3"`/`"4"` as JSON strings would be caught here only if this SDK's own `add` tool refused them — a property of the fixture server, not of this assertion. Silent, on the CG5 rule: a test whose subject is downstream of the requirement does not discharge it.

dispatch_test.exs:84 — `assert resp["error"]["code"] == -32_022` where the check REQUIRES -32601. Driven at `Dispatch.dispatch/3`, below the transport, so there is no HTTP status for the second axis to be about.
